items.title: Beginner 12-Week Foundations Plan
items.summary: Twelve weeks that take a brand-new player from holding a ball to playing a real game situation. Each week pairs one or two short lessons with a parent guide, ten to fifteen minutes of home practice, and a few Baseball IQ questions a child can answer with a parent on the couch.
items.audience: Players aged 4 to 8 in their first or second season, and 9- and 10-year-olds who are new to baseball. Parents do not need any baseball experience; every week tells you exactly what to do and say.

weeks.title: Throwing Basics
weeks.summary: Start with the one skill every other skill depends on. Players learn to hold the ball across the seams, point the glove at the target, step with the opposite foot, and throw. Soft balls and short distances all week.
weeks.coachTip: Say 'point, step, throw' out loud with every rep this week so the words become the player's own self-talk.

weeks.title: Ground Ball Fundamentals
weeks.summary: Players learn the ready position (knees bent, hands out front, weight on the balls of the feet) and how to scoop a rolled ball with the glove on the ground and the throwing hand on top. Parents roll slowly and straight; speed comes much later.
weeks.coachTip: Roll ground balls on grass this week, not dirt, so bad hops never get a chance to scare a new fielder.

weeks.title: Batting Stance
weeks.summary: Before anyone swings hard, players learn to hold the bat with the knocking knuckles lined up and to stand balanced with feet a little wider than the shoulders. Tee setup is taught so home practice is safe and correct.
weeks.coachTip: Check every player's grip and stance before every swing this week; fixing it now saves a season of bad habits.

weeks.title: Catching Basics
weeks.summary: Players learn to catch a soft ball with two hands, thumbs together above the waist and pinkies together below. For children who flinch, the fear-of-the-ball lesson builds comfort with foam balls before anything harder is used.
weeks.coachTip: Toss underhand from six feet to the chest this week and let the glove do less than the two hands do.

weeks.title: Throwing Accuracy
weeks.summary: Now that the motion exists, players aim it. Target throws at a cone, a bucket, or a chalk square on a wall, and a first real game of catch with a partner who gives a glove target. Short sessions with rest days protect young arms.
weeks.coachTip: Make every partner hold a glove target at chest height and praise throws that hit the glove more than throws that are hard.

weeks.title: Baserunning
weeks.summary: Players learn to run through first base instead of stopping on it, and to touch every base in order on the way around. Chalk or sock bases in the yard work perfectly.
weeks.coachTip: Put a cone fifteen feet past first base and call it the finish line so players stop slowing down at the bag.

weeks.title: Fielding and Throwing Together
weeks.summary: The two skills become one play: field the ball in the triangle, bring it to the belly, pull it out of the glove, step, and throw. Players learn the transfer, moving the ball from glove to hand without looking at it.
weeks.coachTip: Teach one piece at a time: field it, freeze, then throw; only when the freeze looks right do you let them connect the two.

weeks.title: Contact Fundamentals
weeks.summary: Players learn to watch the ball all the way to the bat and to take the hands straight to the ball instead of looping. Soft toss from the side and gentle front toss get the swing working against a moving ball.
weeks.coachTip: Ask 'where did the ball hit the bat?' after every swing; a player who can answer is tracking the ball.

weeks.title: Force Plays
weeks.summary: A force play is when a runner must run because the batter is coming to their base, so the fielder only has to touch the base, not tag the runner. Players learn when they are forced to run and how the first baseman receives the throw.
weeks.coachTip: Walk the force play with no ball first: put runners on, ask 'who has to run?', then add a slow roller.

weeks.title: Defensive Responsibilities
weeks.summary: Every fielder has a job on every play, even when the ball is not hit to them. Players learn to call the ball loudly and early, where to move on ground balls, and why nobody stands still while a play happens.
weeks.coachTip: After a coach-hit ground ball, freeze everyone and ask each player where they moved and why before the next ball.

weeks.title: Game Situations
weeks.summary: Players put it together in game-like moments: rounding first on a hit, finding and listening to the base coach, and shaking off a mistake with a next-pitch reset. Expect confusion; it is the week confusion becomes understanding.
weeks.coachTip: Coach bases with two signals only, a windmill for go and two hands up for stop, and make every player find you before each pitch.

weeks.title: Review and Celebration
weeks.summary: A light week that revisits favorite drills as games and finishes with the sportsmanship and effort-over-outcome lessons. Celebrate what each player can do now that they could not do in week one.
weeks.coachTip: Tell each player one specific thing they improved this season, by name, in front of the team.

items.title: Intermediate 12-Week Development Plan
items.summary: Twelve weeks for players who already play catch and field routine ground balls and want to become real infielders, outfielders, and hitters. The plan moves from clean throwing mechanics and footwork into backhands, cutoffs, double plays, tee locations, the two-strike approach, tagging up, situational baserunning, and bunt defense.
items.audience: Players aged 9 to 12 with at least one season of experience, their parents, and volunteer coaches who want a week-by-week map. Home practice is 15 to 20 minutes, two or three days a week, never every day.

weeks.title: Throwing Mechanics and Arm Care
weeks.summary: Rebuild the throw from the ground up: arm circle, elbow at shoulder height, and a real warm-up routine before any hard throwing. Players and parents learn why rest days and pitch limits exist and where to find the league's current rules.
weeks.coachTip: Run the same throwing warm-up at every practice this season so players can lead it themselves by week four.

weeks.title: Footwork: Direction, Quick Feet, and the Crow Hop
weeks.summary: Accuracy lives in the feet. Players learn to line the front shoulder and glove at the target, to use quick infield footwork after fielding, and to crow hop (a hop-step that builds momentum) for longer outfield throws.
weeks.coachTip: Film one throw per player from the side on a phone and show them where their front foot lands; most fix themselves.

weeks.title: Backhands, Forehands, and Approach Angles
weeks.summary: Players learn to approach a ground ball on an angle, to field a backhand (ball to the glove-side's opposite, glove turned fingers down) with the glove-side foot forward, and to make forehand plays on the run. Tennis balls on a driveway are ideal for home work.
weeks.coachTip: Roll backhands slowly enough that players can plant the correct foot; speed hides footwork mistakes.

weeks.title: Cutoffs and Relays
weeks.summary: The cutoff man is the infielder who lines up between the outfielder and the base so a long throw can be caught and redirected. Players learn to field outfield ground balls, to throw to the cutoff's glove side, and where outfielders stand and back up.
weeks.coachTip: Make the cutoff man raise both hands and yell the outfielder's name before every throw this week.

weeks.title: Double Plays and Force Plays
weeks.summary: Players learn to field and throw in one motion, to feed the second baseman or shortstop with a firm underhand flip, and to pivot at second base. The force-play IQ questions make sure everyone knows when the force is on.
weeks.coachTip: Practice the feed and the pivot separately with no runner for a full week before you ever turn a live double play.

weeks.title: Tee Locations and the Load
weeks.summary: Players move the tee to inside, middle, and outside positions and learn that the contact point changes with each one. A small load (a slight shift of weight back before the swing) and keeping the hands inside the ball give the swing power without a long loop.
weeks.coachTip: Put a cone where each tee location's ball should land and let the cones, not you, tell the hitter where contact happened.

weeks.title: Two-Strike Approach and Timing
weeks.summary: With two strikes the job changes: shorten the swing, widen the stance a little, and put the ball in play. Players also learn where the contact point is out front and how to start the swing on time against a real pitcher.
weeks.coachTip: Run every batting-practice round so the last three swings are at an imaginary two-strike count and reward balls put in play.

weeks.title: Tagging Up and Fly-Ball Communication
weeks.summary: Tagging up means a runner waits on the base until a fly ball is caught, then runs. Players learn the rule from the runner's side and the fielder's side: drop steps and angles to the ball, and calling it three times so two fielders never collide.
weeks.coachTip: Put a runner on third during every fly-ball drill so fielders learn to catch and throw in one motion while the runner practices the tag.

weeks.title: Situational Baserunning and Sliding
weeks.summary: Players learn to read the ball off the bat (line drive: freeze; ground ball: go on contact when forced), the runner-on-second reads, and a safe bent-leg slide on grass. Check your league's rules on head-first sliding before teaching anything else.
weeks.coachTip: Teach sliding in socks on wet grass with a towel as the base before anyone slides into a real bag in cleats.

weeks.title: Bunting and Bunt Defense
weeks.summary: Players learn to bunt with the bat angled and the top hand pinching behind the barrel, then flip to defense: the third baseman and first baseman charge, the catcher calls the base, and the pitcher fields anything in front. Catching basics are introduced because the catcher runs this play.
weeks.coachTip: Let the catcher, not you, call the base on every bunt in practice; the habit only forms if the player owns the call.

weeks.title: Game-Ready Defense
weeks.summary: Players learn where every infielder goes on every ground ball, how to play the short hop they want instead of the in-between hop, and how the shortstop runs the infield. The infield fly rule is introduced for older players.
weeks.coachTip: Call outs and runners before every fungo this week so players rehearse the thinking, not just the catching.

weeks.title: Review and the Mental Game
weeks.summary: A lighter week that reviews the season's skills through games and finishes with the mental side: sportsmanship toward opponents and umpires, the flush routine for mistakes, and a pre-game routine players can run on their own.
weeks.coachTip: Ask each player to name one mistake they recovered from this season and how; that conversation is the review.
